title: Step-jump animation — bombers auto-arc onto delta=1 cliffs with crouch+launch+landing animation
intent: Per refined `docs/game-design/terrain-design.md §2.3`: cliffs at height delta = 1 are now traversable via STEP JUMP — bomber automatically arc-jumps onto/off the step with a visible animated hop. Delta ≥ 2 cliffs still block (need Ramp). This refines GDP-2026-05-28-010's blanket 'all cliffs block' rule into a more natural traversal vocabulary: tiny steps (one cell up/down) feel like hopping over a curb; bigger walls feel like real cliffs. Bomber commits to the jump (direction locked mid-arc), Y lerps along a parabola, total time ~0.4s. Animation: brief crouch → launch arc → landing thud. Pairs naturally with GDP-2026-05-28-010 (heights) and the existing dash mechanic (S159) — adds a third traversal verb.
rationale: Source: user request 2026-05-28 — 'я хочу чтоб на ступеньки бомберы запрыгивали с анимацией' + refined `terrain-design.md §2.3` (step jumps for delta=1, ramps for any delta, cliffs for delta≥2 without ramp). Naturally extends the height system from a binary 'cliff blocks' to a graded vocabulary. Variable height becomes much more usable in casual arena authoring: authors can place +1 steps for visual interest without needing ramps everywhere. Marked `should` because variable height (GDP-010) without step-jumps feels constrained — every elevation change forces a ramp tile, which costs arena floor space and visual flexibility.
acceptanceHints: DEPENDS ON: GDP-2026-05-28-010 (variable cell height — Cliff markers + Height components). Cannot ship before.

REVISES the cliff-blocks rule from GDP-010: cliffs with delta=1 are NO LONGER unconditionally blocking; they now allow step-jump traversal. Cliffs with delta≥2 keep the blocking rule unless a Ramp from GDP-011 connects them.
READ FIRST: `docs/game-design/terrain-design.md §2.3` (Step jumps — auto-hop on delta=1 cliff).
TRIGGER MODEL: AUTOMATIC. No new input. Walking into a delta=1 cliff edge: GridMover proceeds (the destination is NOT refused), but the movement becomes a JUMP instead of a walk:
Bomber commits to the destination cell.
Direction queue locks for the 0.4s jump duration.
Transform.position.y arcs along a parabola — start at fromHeight, peak at max(fromHeight, toHeight) + 0.4 cells, end at toHeight.
Transform.position.xz lerps linearly from from-cell to to-cell.
CLIFF-BLOCK REVISION (in GridOccupancySystem):
At cell-tween start, check the height delta to destination:
delta = 0 → normal walk (existing behaviour from GDP-010).
delta = ±1 → STEP JUMP (new path, this story). Mark bomber 'jumping' for the tween duration.
delta ≥ ±2 AND no Ramp → BLOCKED (existing GDP-010 cliff behaviour).
Ramp existence overrides — if a Ramp connects from-to cells, ramp-traversal wins (smooth-glide of GDP-011 — even for delta=1 connections).
JUMP ANIMATION (extend bench-animation-system or its kaboom analog from S104):
Add a new BenchAnimationKind 'jump-step' with sub-phases:
0..0.05s: crouch — bend knees + lower torso ~0.1 cells (squeeze pose).
0.05..0.35s: arc — Y position lerps along parabola, legs extend, torso pitches forward 15°, arms tilt back for balance.
0.35..0.40s: landing — knees bend slightly to absorb (~0.05 cell), torso slight forward dip, then return to neutral.
All limb-pivot rotations driven by jump-step animation system; existing walk/idle stops during jump.
Animation phase advances via jump elapsed time (NOT velocity) — discrete event animation, like reach (GDP-027-014) or dash (S159).
JUMP IS COMMITTED — bomber direction CANNOT be reversed mid-arc:
Player input (Shift+arrow, queued direction) BUFFERED for after the jump completes — applied on landing if still pressed.
Dash mid-jump: refused. Dash starts a new movement, jump is already a movement.
BLOCKING AT DESTINATION:
If destination cell is OCCUPIED by another bomber or a bomb at the moment the jump is initiated: jump REFUSED (treat as cliff edge). Bomber stays at source.

Mid-jump: if destination becomes occupied (e.g. another bomber walks into it during the 0.4s jump): bomber lands ANYWAY at destination but per gameplay-systems.md §2.4 bomber-on-bomber rule, the slower-arrival bomber is bumped back to source.
BLAST INTERACTION (bomber mid-jump caught in blast):

Bomber's logical position during jump = destination cell (gridX, gridZ snap immediately on jump start). Blast hitting destination cell: bomber dies. Ragdoll fires from current arc position (Transform.position) — physics handles the natural fall.
Bomber visibly mid-arc when killed → ragdoll launch direction from blast still works (impulse vector from blast origin).
PATHFINDING EXTENSION:

BFS / A* (bot-ai-system, agent-goto-system) treats delta=1 cliffs as traversable (cost 1.2× compared to flat walk — slightly higher than flat to discourage pure-jump pathing when ramps are available).
delta≥2 cliffs without Ramp still impassable.
Bots will WALK INTO step cliffs and auto-jump — no special bot logic needed.
INTERACTION WITH DASH (S159):
Dash can ALREADY break grid-blocking rules (passes through soft blocks + bombs + bombers). Dash interaction with cliffs:
Dash onto delta=1 step → dash treats it as flat (full 2-cell dash range across the step). The dash's own arc handles the height; no jump animation triggered.
Dash onto delta=2 cliff → blocked at the cliff edge (dash falls back to 1-cell dash, or refused per existing dash rules).
INTERACTION WITH THROW GLOVE (S144) — thrown bomb arcs:
Thrown bomb arc destination uses cell's height. If bomber on H=2 throws over a delta=-2 cliff, bomb lands at H=0 destination.
Unchanged from GDP-010 — already handles per-cell height correctly.
BOMB KICK (S100) — kicked bombs onto/off steps:
Kicked bomb sliding into a delta=1 step → bomb cannot jump steps (bombs are objects, not animated bombers). Bomb stops at the cliff edge (treat as blocking — like kicking into a hard block).
Bomb kicked OFF a step (high to low) → bomb tumbles off, lands at lower cell. Could use a small parabolic arc tween, but ground-snap is fine for v1.
MULTIPLAYER:
Server enforces jump rules per GridOccupancy. Snapshot includes Transform.position.y mid-arc — client interpolator already handles Y smooth-interp.
Animation purely client-side per gameplay-systems.md §12.1 (visual deterministic acceptable).
CAMERA:
Camera from S163 lerps Y. Mid-jump: camera follows bomber's arc Y — smooth.
AUDIO:
New event 'step-jump' — short whoosh on launch + thud on landing. ~150ms total audio.
Voice synth (S110+S158): no new vocal slot. Bomber doesn't speak when jumping.
URL CONFIG:
`?stepJumpDuration=N` overrides default 400ms (clamped 200..800).
`?stepJumps=off` disables — useful for screenshot tests + reverting to GDP-010 cliff-blocks-everything baseline.
UNIT TESTS:
Bomber walks into delta=1 cliff → jump starts; Transform.position.y arcs through parabola; lands at toHeight after ~400ms.
Bomber walks into delta=2 cliff (no ramp) → jump refused (existing behaviour).
Bomber walks into delta=1 cliff with Ramp present → uses ramp (smooth), not jump.
Jump committed: direction-queue input mid-jump buffered, applied on landing.
Pathfinding: BFS includes delta=1 jumps as edges; bot navigates onto a +1 plateau without ramps.
Dash + delta=1 cliff: dash succeeds without jump animation.
Mid-jump blast hit: bomber dies, ragdoll launches from arc position.
Multiplayer: server's snapshot of bomber position mid-jump matches client's local prediction within tolerance.
VISUAL QA (manual):
Bomber walks into a +1 step → visible crouch (brief) → arc up → land thud → continue walk if input still queued.
Animation feels SNAPPY (~0.4s total) — not slow or floaty.
Direction lock mid-jump: pressing reverse during arc doesn't reverse — bomber commits.
PROTOTYPE ARENA:

Update `examples/kaboom-crew/scenes/cliffside.scene.json` from GDP-010: change central plateau from H=2 to H=1 OR keep H=2 and add a few +1 step cells around it. Demonstrates the new auto-jump where steps exist + ramp where bigger climb is needed.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Multi-step jumps (jump from H=0 over H=2 to land at H=4). Single edge only.
Player-controlled jump button (force jump at specific moments). Always automatic.
Bombs auto-tumbling off cliffs (bombs use kick-blocking rule).
Sound-effects per height (different thud for higher landing). Single audio.
Jump from same-height cell (jump-jog feel) — out, walking is walking.
Variable jump height per bomber (recipe-driven). All bombers jump same height.
Combo jumps (jump + dash mid-arc). Sequenced — one at a time.
Wall-jumps (bouncing off vertical surfaces). Steps only.
